title: Fix literal exclamation marks in gitignore patterns
body:
Fixes #334711

Ignore patterns containing a literal `!` can include or exclude the wrong file. With `*.txt` followed by `!important!.txt`, the shared parser currently re-includes `important.txt` and excludes `important!.txt`.

Recognize negation only at the start of a pattern, remove only that prefix, and unescape a leading `\!` when converting the remaining pattern to a glob. This also preserves negated character classes such as `[!a].txt`.

The parser is used by browser local-folder search and by Explorer when `explorer.excludeGitIgnore` is enabled. Existing rule-order and directory-traversal semantics are unchanged.

### Validation

On macOS arm64 with Node 24.18.0:

- 72 Electron unit tests passed across the ignore parser and glob suites, including 8 regression tests for literal exclamation marks, directories, negation, escaping, character classes, and case-insensitive matching.
- 27 file/directory/nested-path cases agree with `git check-ignore`; 17 of those cases disagree on the base revision.
- Client transpilation, changed-file ESLint, hygiene, and `git diff --check` passed.

```sh
npm run transpile-client
scripts/test.sh --runGlob 'vs/{workbench/services/search/test/common/ignoreFile,base/test/common/glob}.test.js'
npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/services/search/common/ignoreFile.ts src/vs/workbench/services/search/test/common/ignoreFile.test.ts
npm run precommit -- src/vs/workbench/services/search/common/ignoreFile.ts src/vs/workbench/services/search/test/common/ignoreFile.test.ts
```

### Manual verification

The automated verification above exercises the core parser; the following UI checks have not been run:

1. Create `important!.txt`, `important.txt`, and `other.txt`, each containing the same search term.
2. Add a `.gitignore` containing `*.txt` followed by `!important!.txt`.
3. In browser local-folder search, keep ignore-file filtering enabled. Only `important!.txt` should contribute a search result.
4. In Explorer, enable `explorer.excludeGitIgnore`. With the fixture files closed in editors, only `important!.txt` should remain visible among the three text files.

title: Ignore parser treats literal exclamation marks as negation
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Reproduced in the core parser without loading extensions. Browser and Explorer UI verification has not been performed for this report.

- VS Code Version: source `main` at `fc0a9e94576224c89cc08d390b38ab760a261f1f` (`1.138.0` development version)
- OS Version: macOS 27.0 (26A5425a), arm64; Node 24.18.0

The shared `IgnoreFile` parser treats an exclamation mark anywhere in a `.gitignore` pattern as negation, then removes every exclamation mark. This can exclude the intended exception and include a different filename instead.

For example:

```gitignore
*.txt
!important!.txt
```

The first `!` negates the rule; the second belongs to the filename. The parser currently re-includes `important.txt` instead of `important!.txt`.

### Steps to reproduce in the core parser

1. Check out the source revision above and install the repository dependencies.
2. Run `npm run transpile-client`.
3. From the repository root, run:

```sh
node --input-type=module <<'JS'
import { IgnoreFile } from './out/vs/workbench/services/search/common/ignoreFile.js';

const ignore = new IgnoreFile('*.txt\n!important!.txt', '/');
for (const file of ['/important!.txt', '/important.txt']) {
  console.log(file, ignore.isArbitraryPathIgnored(file, false));
}
JS
```

| File | Expected `isArbitraryPathIgnored` | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/important!.txt` | `false` | `true` |
| `/important.txt` | `true` | `false` |

Other inputs exposing the same classification problem are `important!.txt` (a literal filename to exclude), `\!important.txt` (an escaped leading exclamation mark), and `[!a].txt` (a negated character class).

### Affected code paths

- Browser local-folder file and text search reads `.gitignore` and `.ignore` through this parser in `localFileSearch.ts`.
- Explorer filtering uses the same parser when `explorer.excludeGitIgnore` is enabled, including on desktop (`explorerViewer.ts`).

Native ripgrep search uses a separate implementation. The behavior above was reproduced directly in the shared parser, rather than inferred from a desktop search result.

The [Git pattern documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore#_pattern_format) describes negation as a prefix and permits escaping a literal leading exclamation mark. Comparing 27 file, directory, and nested-path cases with `git check-ignore` found 17 mismatches before the proposed fix and none afterward.

Related: #156077 concerns re-including directories. This report reproduces with files at the root and literal exclamation marks, independently of that directory-traversal behavior.

title: Preserve literal dollars in case-converted search replacements
body:
Workspace Search reinterprets dollar sequences in case-converted captures as replacement syntax. Searching `^(foo.*)$` in `foo$1` and replacing with `\U$1` currently produces `FOOfoo$1`; this change produces `FOO$1` in both the preview and the saved file.

Fixes #334709.

Collect the converted capture separately and escape its literal dollars before appending it to the replacement template. Other capture substitutions continue through the existing path. Add seven regression cases covering capture references, whole-match/prefix/suffix references, escaped dollars, named-reference text, and mixed converted/unconverted captures.

Related to #299365 and #326451, which handle `$$` entered in the replacement field. That PR does not cover dollar sequences in case-converted captured text. This branch is based directly on `main` and does not depend on #334698.

### Validation

On macOS arm64 with Node 24.18.0:

- All seven new regression cases fail on the unmodified implementation and pass with this change.
- 258 related Electron unit tests pass; three existing/platform-specific tests are skipped.
- Changed-file ESLint, hygiene, and `git diff --check` pass.
- With fresh profiles and `--disable-extensions`, verified the Search view preview and actual Replace All edits in both baseline and fixed Code OSS: `foo$1`, `foo$&`, and `foo$$` now become `FOO$1`, `FOO$&`, and `FOO$$`.

```sh
scripts/test.sh --runGlob 'vs/{workbench/services/search,workbench/contrib/search,editor/contrib/find}/test/**/*.test.js'
npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/services/search/common/replace.ts src/vs/workbench/services/search/test/common/replace.test.ts
npm run precommit -- src/vs/workbench/services/search/common/replace.ts src/vs/workbench/services/search/test/common/replace.test.ts
```

title: Search: case conversion reinterprets literal dollar sequences in captured text
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
Workspace search corrupts captured text containing replacement syntax when a case modifier is applied. The dollar sequences below are part of the file content, so changing case should preserve them literally.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes. Reproduced with `--disable-extensions` and a fresh Code OSS profile.

- VS Code version: Code OSS 1.138.0 development build from `main` at `fc0a9e94576224c89cc08d390b38ab760a261f1f`.
- OS: macOS 27.0, arm64.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a folder containing a saved `dollars.txt` file with these three lines:

   ```text
   foo$1
   foo$&
   foo$$
   ```

2. Open **Replace in Files** (the Search view), enable **Use Regular Expression**, and leave **Preserve Case** off.
3. Search for `^(foo.*)$` and replace with `\U$1`.
4. Inspect the replacement preview, then use **Replace All**.

| Input | Expected | Actual preview and saved file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `foo$1` | `FOO$1` | `FOOfoo$1` |
| `foo$&` | `FOO$&` | `FOOfoo$&` |
| `foo$$` | `FOO$$` | `FOO$` |

### Cause and related reports

`replaceWithCaseOperations` converts the captured text and inserts it directly into the replacement template passed to `String.replace`. Dollar sequences in that captured text are consequently interpreted again as replacement syntax. Core regression cases also reproduce this with prefix/suffix references and named-reference text.

Related: #299365 and #326451 concern `$$` entered directly in the replacement field. This report concerns dollar sequences in the captured **file content** after case conversion. I ran the `foo$1` and `foo$$` cases against #326451's head (`6a830ff084777cc45b024028a2dd52dce8c6c842`); both still produce the incorrect results above.

title: Fix search replacement case operations on short and empty captures
body:
Workspace search replacement can throw when stacked case modifiers outnumber the characters in a capture, and can insert literal case-modifier text when an optional capture is unmatched. For example, searching `^(?:([a-z]+)_)?([a-z]+)$` and replacing with `\u$1\u$2` changes `name` to `\uName` in the Search view, while editor find/replace correctly produces `Name`.

Fixes #334697.

Bound case operations by the capture length and treat existing empty or unmatched capture groups as empty strings. Preserve the existing handling of references to nonexistent groups. Add six regression cases for short captures, empty captures, optional groups, and subsequent groups.

### How to test

In **Replace in Files**, enable regex and leave **Preserve Case** off:

- In a saved file containing `user_name`, `name`, and `id` on separate lines, search `^(?:([a-z]+)_)?([a-z]+)$` and replace with `\u$1\u$2`. Both the preview and Replace All should produce `UserName`, `Name`, and `Id`.
- In a saved file containing `url`, `id`, and `x` on separate lines, search `^([a-z]{1,3})$` and replace with `\u\u\u$1`. Enable Match Case. Both the preview and Replace All should produce `URL`, `ID`, and `X` without an exception.

### Validation

On macOS arm64 with Node 24.18.0:

- 257 related Electron unit tests passed; 3 existing/platform-specific skips.
- 83 search integration tests passed.
- Client typecheck, changed-file ESLint, and hygiene passed.
- Reproduced the incorrect preview and actual file edits in installed VS Code 1.136.1. Verified correct preview and actual Replace All edits in a locally built Code OSS for optional captures and stacked modifiers on short captures.
- Full build passed after regeneration of a pre-existing stale `monaco.d.ts`; the unrelated generated change was restored and excluded, and the exact branch then passed client typecheck.

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

Search view case modifiers mishandle empty or short numbered capture groups. The equivalent replacement in the editor's find widget works correctly.

- VS Code version: 1.136.1
- OS: macOS 27.0, arm64
- Also reproduced directly against the core search replacement implementation at current `main`, `fc0a9e94576224c89cc08d390b38ab760a261f1f`.

Extension isolation: reproduced in core replacement tests without loading extensions. The installed-app UI reproduction below was with extensions enabled; a separate UI run with all extensions disabled has not been verified.

### Reproduction: optional capture

1. Open a folder containing a saved text file with these lines:

   ```text
   user_name
   name
   id
   ```

2. Open **Replace in Files** in the Search view (not the editor's single-file find widget).
3. Enable **Use Regular Expression**. Leave **Preserve Case** off.
4. Search for `^(?:([a-z]+)_)?([a-z]+)$`.
5. Replace with `\u$1\u$2`.
6. Inspect the replacement preview, then run Replace All.

Expected saved contents:

```text
UserName
Name
Id
```

Actual preview and saved contents:

```text
UserName
\uName
\uId
```

The first group exists but does not participate in the matches for `name` and `id`; its case modifier should not become literal output.

### Related boundary case: stacked modifiers on a short capture

Search `^([a-z]{1,3})$` and replace with `\u\u\u$1` on separate lines containing `url`, `id`, and `x`. The expected results are `URL`, `ID`, and `X`. In the current core search replacement implementation, `id` and `x` throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toUpperCase')` because case operations continue past the end of the capture. The editor's find/replace implementation handles these inputs.

### Related reports checked

- #19740 concerns editor find/replace inserting literal `undefined` for an unmatched group without case modifiers. Here, Search view retains the case modifier itself, and editor find/replace produces the expected result.
- #140734 concerns newlines being dropped from multiline replacements using case modifiers. These examples use single-line matches and empty or short captures; the existing newline regression test passes.
- #150070, which was referred to #128134, concerns replacements using lookahead and newline matching with `$1$2$2`. That replacement has no case modifiers and takes the unchanged replacement path.
- #288968 adds named capture group support. These examples use numbered groups; that PR retains the empty-capture check and unbounded case-operation loop involved here.

Workspace search case-modifier support was introduced in #105101.

A small fix with six regression tests is prepared on https://github.com/Suzu1Dev/vscode/tree/fix/search-replace-short-captures. The fixed build passes the same preview and actual Replace All scenarios, 257 related Electron unit tests (3 existing skips), and 83 search integration tests.

title: sessions: measure and unblock V3 onboarding GitHub personalization

labels.name: release-cherry-pick
labels.description: Automated cherry-pick between release and main branches

body:
## Why

The V3 new-session onboarding personalizes its 3 prompt options with GitHub items (assigned issues, authored PRs with conflicts / failing CI / unresolved review comments), falling back to standard options.

Analysis of experiment `f716301b` over 3 weeks and ~780k users found that, restricted to users with a resolved GitHub repository who saw the options widget (222,470 impressions):

- **61.0%** timed out with zero GitHub options
- **~9.4%** saw at least one GitHub option (only **0.17%** saw a full 3/3 set)
- **29.6%** got all-standard options

And we could not measure *how* badly, because `fallbackReason` was only set to `'none'` when all 3 slots were GitHub — so a widget with 2 real GitHub issues logged identically to one with zero. That blind spot covered 81% of impressions.

The root cause of the timeouts is that per-stage budgets could exceed the total budget: the PR chain was summary(5s) → review(4s) = 9s, with repository resolution also inside the same 10s budget.

## Telemetry

Additive only — existing field names and values are emitted in the same situations, so live dashboards keep working.

`onboarding.promptStrategy` gains:

| Field | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `gitHubOptionCount` | How many of the 3 slots were actually GitHub items — closes the main blind spot |
| `candidatesFound` | Pre-truncation count: "repo has nothing" vs "found items but were too slow" |
| `lookupDurationMs` | Total lookup time (plumbed from the value the code already computed for logging) |
| `repositoryMs`, `issueSummaryMs`, `issueLinkageMs`, `prSummaryMs`, `prReviewMs` | Which stage is actually slow |
| `issueSummaryOutcome`, `issueLinkageOutcome`, `prSummaryOutcome`, `prReviewOutcome` | Per-stage outcome, so "issues succeeded, PRs timed out" is distinguishable from total failure |
| `timedOutStage` | Which stage was in flight when the total budget expired |

`onboarding.promptOptionInteraction` gains `optionIndex` and `optionKindsShown`, making a true per-option CTR computable — today "implementFeature is most picked" is confounded with it being almost always present.

Both events gain a shared `impressionId`, so they can be joined per impression instead of on `DevDeviceId`, which is lossy for devices with multiple impressions.

Also splits the overloaded `noCandidate` — it meant both "no composer available" (an infra bug) and "lookup returned nothing" (a data outcome). The former is now `noComposer`.

**Privacy:** bounded categories and counts only. No issue/PR titles, URLs, numbers, repository names or prompt text. Every numeric has `isMeasurement: true`.

## Latency

`totalMs` stays at 10s.

1. **Publish issue candidates before linkage.** Linkage exists only to filter out issues that already have linked PRs, so a slow linkage call was discarding issues we already held.
2. **Review-thread enrichment off the critical path.** It fired N parallel lookups after a summary to produce `githubPRComments` — 30 selections, 0.37% of all picks — while `githubIssue` (the most-picked GitHub option) is the cheapest to fetch. The budget was being spent inversely to user value. It can now only refine, never delay first paint.
3. **Rebalanced sub-budgets** to `summaryMs: 4_000, linkageMs: 1_500, reviewMs: 3_000`. The issue and PR chains run concurrently under `Promise.all`, so the worst case for timed lookups is `max(4_000+1_500, 4_000+3_000) = 7_000ms`, leaving ~3s for repository resolution and rendering. Repository resolution has no budget of its own and a workspace change restarts the chain; both are bounded only by the `totalMs` race, and the comment on the constant says so rather than asserting a tighter bound than the code has.
4. **Streaming.** The 3 standard options are painted immediately and slots are replaced as GitHub items arrive, instead of blocking first paint on the whole lookup. Beyond timeouts, this also addresses V3's ~17pp tour-reach deficit versus V2.

## API change

`INewSessionPromptOptionsController.resolve` gains an optional progress callback:

```ts
export type NewSessionPromptOptionsProgress = (state: NewSessionPromptOptionsState) => boolean;

resolve(token: CancellationToken, progress?: NewSessionPromptOptionsProgress): Promise<NewSessionPromptOptionsState>;
```

Additive and optional, so existing callers are unaffected. It returns `boolean` rather than `void` deliberately: the composer refuses late updates while the user is already acting on the options, and the runner needs to know that so interaction telemetry describes what was actually rendered.

## Notes for reviewers

The streaming path has three subtle interactions that are each covered by a test that fails without its fix:

- `_renderedPromptOptions` is reset per `resolve`, not per `run`. `newChatWidget` calls `refreshPromptOptions()` on every workspace change against the same runner, and a per-run reset made the second refresh compare against the previous refresh's final set — suppressing first paint entirely in exactly the all-standard case this PR targets.
- `_promptOptionsSelected` is set at the *start* of `selectOption`, not in `onDidSelectOption`. The widget only reports a selection after the 2.5s prompt animation completes; a streamed update in that window would clear the selection and leave every option `aria-disabled`.
- The runner commits `_renderedPromptOptions` only when the composer accepted the update, so `optionIndex` / `optionKindsShown` can never describe options the user never saw.

`impressionId` is regenerated per `run`, not per `resolve`: strategy telemetry is emitted once per run, so a per-resolve id would orphan interaction events from any strategy event.

- `scripts\test.bat --grep "NewSession"` → **93 passing**, 0 failing

- Distribution of `gitHubOptionCount` (0/1/2/3) — the true personalization rate, vs today's binary
- Per-stage p50/p95 latency and timeout rate, attributing the 61% bucket to `repository` vs `prSummary` vs `prReview`
- `candidatesFound == 0` vs `candidatesFound > gitHubOptionCount` — "nothing to show" vs "found more than we could show"

Minimal — removes redundant imports only; no logic, telemetry, or runtime behavior changes.

title: imageCarousel: add copy, save and source actions
body:
Fixes #329065.

## Changes
- Add Copy Image, Save Media As, Open Source, and Reveal in Explorer View through the existing modal editor toolbar and an image-area context menu (including Shift+F10).
- Support Ctrl/Cmd+C without intercepting text input. Copy rasterizes to PNG. Save writes the cached preview bytes without additional re-encoding; web uses the existing download helper.
- Detect the actual encoded MIME for chat attachment bytes and correct the suggested export extension. Chat may already have resized/re-encoded an attachment (for example GIF to PNG), so exporting that preview does not reconstruct the original file or animation.
- Preserve real file/provider source URIs, excluding generated content, data identities, and pasted-image cache references.
- Open sources in the main editor group. Reveal uses the registered Explorer view in either workbench and suppresses auto-reveal during modal close/explicit selection, restoring its previous mode in finally.

## Review scope
No clipboard platform API, new service, editor-input selection model, CSS, settings, or accessibility-provider changes. Selection stays in the pane; the existing Blob cache retains the displayed bytes. Image signature detection is extracted from the existing base image helper and reused instead of duplicating parsers.

The optional Save As shortcut remains omitted because it conflicts with the modal keyboard guard. Save is keyboard-accessible through the standard toolbar/context menu without changing shared editor routing.

## Refresh and validation
- Merged upstream `main` at `a47dab6a0a5` without rewriting published commits (`93ea7d572a8`).
- Addressed all three review findings in `4ffc1202a0a`, with replies and resolved threads.
- Targeted Electron suites: **89 passing**.
- Targeted Chromium suites: **86 passing, 2 pending** (native Save dialog tests are Electron-only).
- Coverage includes actual GIF-to-PNG resizing, pasted cache provenance, encoded-format detection, corrected export filenames, and auto-reveal restoration on success and failure.
- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run transpile-client`, hygiene, and `git diff --check`: **passed**. The previous Sessions compile diagnostics are gone after syncing upstream.

title: Refresh markdown preview html before a hidden panel is rebuilt
body:
Fixes #271233
Part of #265277

Several reports in those issues describe the same sequence: the preview updates correctly while it is visible, the user switches to another tab and back, and the preview shows the content from before the update. This applies to the dynamic preview (`markdown.showPreview`) and to the `vscode.markdown.preview.editor` custom editor, with edits made in VS Code as well as with files overwritten on disk.

### Root cause

`MarkdownPreview` applies updates made while the panel is visible by posting an `updateContent` message to the webview, and leaves `webview.html` untouched. Neither preview uses `retainContextWhenHidden`, so VS Code discards the webview when the panel is hidden and rebuilds it from `webview.html` when the panel is revealed. That html is whatever the last full render produced, so every update applied through `updateContent` since then is lost on reveal. Nothing in the preview reacts to the panel being hidden, and the version check in `#updatePreview` keeps a later refresh from re-rendering unchanged content.

### Fix

- Track whether `webview.html` is behind what the webview shows (`#webviewHtmlOutOfDate`).
- When the panel is hidden while the html is behind, request a forced refresh, which goes through the existing full render path and brings `webview.html` up to date before the panel can be revealed. Panels that never received an in-place update, and panels updated while hidden (which already re-render fully), are unaffected.
- If the panel is hidden while an in-place update is still rendering, the update requests the forced refresh itself: the hide event found the html up to date and scheduled nothing, and the webview the message was meant for is already gone.
- `refresh(true)` now keeps its force flag when an update is already scheduled. Before, a forced refresh requested while the 300 ms throttle timer was pending was silently downgraded to a regular update.

### Verification

Measured by driving the extension from source in Insiders 1.137.0-insider (de8cc55dae) with `--extensionDevelopmentPath`, reading the rendered `.markdown-body` text of the preview iframe over the remote debugging port after each step. "hidden" reads as no preview iframe at all, which is the webview being discarded.

| Scenario | Step | main (42b37b7a) | with this change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dynamic preview, file overwritten on disk while visible, tab switch | 1 preview opened | D1-A | D1-A |
| | 2 after external write | D1-B | D1-B |
| | 3 preview hidden behind another tab | hidden | hidden |
| | 4 preview tab shown again | **D1-A (stale)** | D1-B |
| Dynamic preview, edit + save in a text editor, tab switch | 1 preview opened | D1-A | D1-A |
| | 2 after edit and save | D1-C | D1-C |
| | 3 preview hidden behind another tab | hidden | hidden |
| | 4 preview tab shown again | **D1-A (stale)** | D1-C |
| Dynamic preview, file overwritten while hidden (control) | 1 preview opened | D1-A | D1-A |
| | 2 preview tab shown after the hidden write | D1-D | D1-D |
| `vscode.markdown.preview.editor`, file overwritten on disk while visible, tab switch | 1 editor opened | D1-A | D1-A |
| | 2 after external write | D1-E | D1-E |
| | 3 editor hidden behind another tab | hidden | hidden |
| | 4 editor tab shown again | **D1-A (stale)** | D1-E |

The new tests in `src/test/preview.test.ts` revive a `DynamicMarkdownPreview` on a real webview panel. The first applies an edit while the panel is visible, hides the panel behind a text editor and asserts that `webview.html` catches up; it fails on main at that last assertion and passes with this change. The second holds the in-place render of an edit, hides the panel while it is in flight, releases the render and asserts the same; it fails when the branch in `#updateWebviewContent` is removed. The third makes a further edit so a regular refresh is pending, hides and re-reveals the panel, and asserts the reveal still gets a full reload. The full markdown-language-features suite passes (99 tests, 1 skipped).

### Related issues

- #271233 is this sequence exactly (modify the file, hide the preview behind another editor in the same group, show it again). The later comment there about closing and reopening the preview is a different mechanism, see below.
- #165188 (closed as a duplicate of #147718) and #244328 (closed) describe the same tab-switch sequence.
- #331900, #194421 and #316067 are about a preview that is closed and reopened, or opened fresh, showing old content. The webview is created new in those flows, so this change does not apply; #332081 and #333712 target that path.

### Relation to the other open PRs

- #308427 (`refresh()` when the panel becomes visible, claims to fix #271233) calls the non-forced `refresh()` of the base class. The document version has not changed since the in-place update, so `#updatePreview` returns at the version check and `webview.html` stays stale. Measured with that diff applied on top of 1.128.0: step 4 of the first scenario above still shows D1-A.
- #166932 (`refresh()` when the dynamic preview becomes inactive, 2022) goes through `DynamicMarkdownPreview.refresh()`, which is forced, so it does fix the dynamic preview (steps 4 above render D1-B and D1-C with it). It reloads the whole page every time the preview loses focus, whether or not anything changed, which is the concern raised in its review, and it does not cover `vscode.markdown.preview.editor` (step 4 of the last scenario stays D1-A). This change reloads only when an in-place update has actually happened and covers both previews.
- #307245 defers refreshes while the panel is hidden and re-renders on reveal only if a change arrived while hidden. It does not change what happens to updates applied before the hide, so the two changes are independent.
- #333712 (identity-aware `PreviewDocumentVersion.equals`) and #332081 (token cache identity) address refreshes being skipped while the preview is visible; no overlap. #316756 removes the watcher guard for documents VS Code already tracks; it does not change what a hidden panel is rebuilt from, so the tab-switch case above stays stale with it.

title: Fix C/C++ auto-indent after brace-less if/for/while/else (#43244)
body:
## Fixes #43244

JS, TS, and PHP already indent the line following a brace-less `if`/`for`/`while`/`else` via `indentNextLinePattern` in their `language-configuration.json` (added in #209038 / #251465 and follow-ups). The `cpp` language configuration (shared by `c`, `cpp`, and `cuda-cpp`) already has the *matching* outdent-after-single-statement `onEnterRule`, but never got the `indentNextLinePattern` that triggers the initial indent, so today:

```c
if (condition)
<Enter> // does not indent, unlike JS/TS/PHP
```

This has been reported repeatedly in #43244 since 2018 (e.g. "This also applies to C/C++/D, as well" and a comment as recent as June 2025 asking specifically about C), but only JS/TS/PHP ever received the fix.

### Change

Adds the same `indentNextLinePattern` already shipped for JS/TS/PHP to `extensions/cpp/language-configuration.json`:

```json
"indentNextLinePattern": {
    "pattern": "^\\s*(((else ?)?if|for|while)\\s*\\(.*\\)\\s*|else\\s*)$"
}
```

This is the exact same pattern used as the `previousLineText` of the existing outdent `onEnterRule` in this same file, so the two rules are now consistent with each other and with the JS/TS/PHP configs.

### Testing

`shouldIncrease`/`shouldDecrease`/`shouldIndentNextLine` (src/vs/editor/common/languages/supports/indentRules.ts) are driven purely by these regexes with no language-specific code, so no engine changes are needed. I verified the new pattern against representative C/C++ lines (`if (x)`, `else if (x)`, `for (...)`, `while (...)`, `else`, brace/one-line/comment negatives) against the exact regex used by the engine — all matched as expected, mirroring the already-shipped JS/TS/PHP behavior.

I wasn't able to spin up a full Electron build in my environment to record a GIF, but happy to add one if a maintainer can confirm the expected behavior manually or point me at the fastest local-build path for a quick sanity check.

title: terminal: do not buffer local pty events that have no IPC client
body:
Fixes #328885

## Problem

The main process grows with terminal output until V8's ~4 GB heap limit and crashes, closing every window at once. `ProxyChannel.fromService` wraps every `on*` property of a service in an eager `Event.buffer` (`src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts`) that keeps each emission until the first client listens. The `TerminalIpcChannels.LocalPty` channel registered in `app.ts` exposes `PtyHostService`, and a window never listens to the seven `IPtyService` events over it: it consumes them over the direct message port to the pty host (`TerminalIpcChannels.PtyHostWindow`, `localTerminalBackend.ts`). So the main process archived every `onProcessData` chunk for the lifetime of the session.

The pty host and the remote server do not leak by this path: the main process subscribes to the pty host's events as soon as it connects, and `RemoteTerminalChannel.listen` hands events out directly.

## Fix

- Register the channel with `unbufferedEvents` for the `IPtyService` events, the mechanism #328535 introduced for `onDidBlurMainWindow`. The five `IPtyHostController` events stay buffered, those do have a client on this channel.
- `ptyServiceEvents` lives next to `IPtyService` and is exhaustive by type (`satisfies Record<..., true>`): adding an event to the interface without listing it does not compile.
- The registration lives in `createLocalPtyChannel`, so a test can build the very channel production builds.

## Tests

`src/vs/platform/terminal/test/node/ptyHostService.test.ts`:
- every `on*` property of `PtyHostService` is either an `IPtyService` or an `IPtyHostController` event, reflected the way `fromService` does;
- the channel has no listener on any `IPtyService` event before a client asks for it, and a client who asks gets live events without a backlog.

Each guard was checked against its mutation: removing a name from the constant fails to compile, adding an `on*` to the class fails the first test, dropping `unbufferedEvents` from the factory fails the second.

## How to test manually

Open a few integrated terminals producing heavy output (for example `yes | head -c 500M`) and watch the private bytes of the main process. Before this change they grow with the output and never come back; after it they stay flat.

A general cap for `Event.buffer`, as defence in depth for any `fromService` channel with an unconsumed event, is a possible follow-up. This PR is deliberately limited to the channel that leaks.

title: Agent Merge: retry timed-out CI jobs once before giving up
body:
Testing #334491

## Description
Agent Merge should automatically retry a failed required CI check at least once when the failure is a timeout that may be caused by transient infrastructure problems, rather than immediately giving up.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Enable Agent Merge with permission to fix failed required CI checks.
2. Have a required CI job fail due to a timeout.
3. Observe how Agent Merge handles the failure.

## Expected
- Detect a timeout failure that may be infrastructure-related.
- Automatically rerun the failed job once before giving up, without requiring a code change.
- If the retry also fails, stop automatic retries and surface the remaining failure for investigation.
- Track the retry across Agent Merge turns so the same failure does not trigger an unlimited retry loop.

A timeout is not necessarily a code regression; one bounded retry can recover from a transient runner or infrastructure issue. A timeout alone should not be treated as proof that the failure is infrastructure-related.

## Actual / requested improvement
Agent Merge can give up on a timeout failure without first attempting a retry. Provide a bounded automatic retry before reporting that it cannot proceed.

title: Scope MCP tool availability to referenced servers only
body:
## Description

Fixes #334569 — MCP tool calls intermittently rejected with "disabled by the user" while the cache shows enabled and the server log shows execution.

**This is the conservative alternative to #334641.** Both PRs fix the same root cause; this one scopes the fix to the **referenced MCP server only**, preserving the authorization boundary. Maintainers can choose either approach (see the issue for the comparison).

### Root Cause

In **ask mode**, MCP tools can only enter `availableTools` via `request.toolReferences` (the `askAgentToolFilter` in `askAgentIntent.ts`). When the user references an MCP server (via the `@` picker), the toolset is expanded into a **static snapshot** at request-parse time (`chatRequestParser.ts`):

```ts
const value = Array.from(toolset.getTools()).map(t => ...);
```

MCP servers connect and discover their tools **asynchronously**. If the request is parsed while discovery is still in progress, the snapshot only contains the tools registered up to that point. Tools discovered later are registered in the tools service but never enter `availableTools` — the model's calls to them are rejected with `Tool ... is currently disabled by the user`.

### Fix (scoped to the referenced server)

In `askAgentIntent.ts`:

1. **Compute the set of referenced MCP servers** from `request.toolReferences` — for each referenced tool that is currently registered with an `LanguageModelToolMCPSource`, add that server's identity (label + name) to the set.
2. **In the filter**, a currently-registered MCP tool is enabled **only if it belongs to one of the referenced servers** (matching via `LanguageModelToolMCPSource`). Tools from other MCP servers the user never referenced stay unavailable — the authorization boundary is preserved.

```ts
const referencedMcpServerKeys = new Set<string>();
for (const ref of request.toolReferences) {
    const referencedTool = toolsService.getTool(ref.name);
    const source = referencedTool?.source;
    if (source instanceof LanguageModelToolMCPSource) {
        referencedMcpServerKeys.add(mcpServerKey(source.label, source.name));
    }
}
```

### Why not just enable all MCP tools (see #334641)

The request snapshot is both a timing mechanism *and* an **authorization boundary**: it limits the model to the servers the user explicitly referenced. Enabling every `mcp`-tagged tool whenever the user references *any* MCP server would expose the tools of all configured MCP servers (e.g. in a multi-server setup, referencing Firefox would also expose an unrelated IDA/GitKraken server's tools). This PR fixes the timing issue without widening that boundary.

### Validation

- `askAgentIntent.spec.ts` — 8 unit tests covering:
  - codesearch-tagged and directly referenced tools still included
  - MCP tools of a **referenced** server included (snapshot case)
  - MCP tools of a **non-referenced** server **excluded**
  - MCP tools without a resolvable source excluded (conservative fallback)
  - no references / non-MCP references → MCP tools excluded
- All 8 tests pass (`vitest run src/extension/intents/test/node/askAgentIntent.spec.ts`).

### Related

- Issue: #334569
- Alternative fix: #334641

## Overview

## Overview
Currently, the extension activation and configuration change listener rely on hardcoded `if-else` blocks for individual features (e.g., `NpmUpToDateFeature`). As the codebase grows and new extension features are introduced, this approach becomes difficult to scale and maintain.

## Proposed Solution
Introduce a centralized **Feature Registry** pattern using a declarative array (`FeatureDefinition`) combined with a dynamic `Map<string, vscode.Disposable>`. 

* **Scalability:** New features can be registered seamlessly via configuration keys and factory functions without modifying core lifecycle logic.
* **Encapsulation:** Configuration synchronization, initialization, and disposal logic are handled centrally and uniformly.
* **Cleanup:** Guarantees proper memory management and resource disposal through `vscode.Disposable` mapping.

## Changes Included
- Added `FeatureDefinition` interface mapping config keys to instantiation factories.
- Replaced manual property checks with iterative feature synchronization over a registry array.
- Improved `dispose` routine to clear active feature instances cleanly.

title: Agent host renders nothing for a skill that runs in a subagent
body:
A skill invoked as a subagent produces no visible output at all. The turn runs for as long as the
skill takes, renders an empty bubble, and completes. The work is real and its result is recoverable
from the SDK transcript afterwards, so nothing is lost except the user's ability to see it.

## Version

- VS Code 1.136.1, commit `a44adf7f53e00964ab890f9f8758a334f1fc15bc`
- Dev container, `linux-arm64` server bundle
- Claude agent host, Claude Code CLI 2.1.239

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a chat against a workspace with uncommitted or unpushed changes.
2. Run the built in `/code-review`, which runs its reviewer as a subagent.
3. Watch the chat for the duration of the review.

## What happens

The turn shows a spinner and produces nothing. When the review finishes, the turn completes with an
empty response.

On one measured run lasting 10 minutes 8 seconds and making 40 tool calls, the workbench received
exactly these actions on the chat channel:

| Action | Count |
| --- | --- |
| `chat/turnStarted` | 1 |
| `chat/usage` | 1, reporting 0 input and 0 output tokens |
| `chat/turnComplete` | 1, `duration: 607762` |
| `chat/responsePart` | 0 |
| `chat/toolCallStart` | 0 |

The review produced 13.6 KB of findings, recovered afterwards from
`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<sessionId>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`. While it ran, that transcript grew
continuously, so the work was plainly in progress the whole time the UI showed nothing.

## Why

A skill that runs in a subagent is spawned by the skill runner rather than by a `Task` tool call, so
its sidechain agent has no tool-use id. Comparing the two shapes:

```
Task spawned      {"agentType":"...","description":"...","toolUseId":"toolu_...","spawnDepth":1}
skill spawned     {"agentType":"general-purpose"}
```

`SubagentRegistry` is keyed on that tool-use id, so a skill spawned agent is never registered, no
subagent chat is opened, and nothing about it reaches the workbench.

Because the parent model never runs in this shape, the turn reports zero tokens and the entire
product of the turn arrives on the SDK `result` message. In `ClaudeSdkPipeline`, the `result` branch
settles the queue head, logs the uuid, and discards `result` without reading it, so that text is
never surfaced.

## Suggested fix

When a turn completes having emitted no response parts, surface the `result` message's text as a
response part. Guarding on the turn having spent no model tokens is enough to avoid duplicating a
normal turn, whose result text merely repeats the assistant message already streamed. A local patch
along those lines renders the output correctly, verified against both a skill subagent turn and
ordinary turns.

Two things that fix does not cover:

- **Progress while the skill runs.** Nothing about these agents reaches the host during the run, so
  there is nothing to render until the result arrives.
- **Surviving a reload.** The host keeps no chat content of its own. `session.db` holds `turns`,
  `turn_usage`, `session_metadata` and `chat_drafts`, with no table for response parts, and a chat
  re-renders by replaying what the CLI streams on resume. A skill subagent turn leaves no assistant
  message in the CLI transcript, so after a reload there is nothing to replay and the turn is empty
  again.

## Related symptom, same root cause

Because the parent model never runs, the CLI writes no user or assistant message and never persists
the conversation. Cancelling such a turn in a new chat leaves a transcript holding only a file
snapshot and a couple of queue records. Every later prompt in that chat resumes a session id the CLI
does not know:

```
[Claude] session <id>: resume rebuild agent=(none)
[Claude SDK stderr] No conversation found with session ID: <id>
```

The chat is then unusable permanently. A chat that already has history is unaffected, so this only
bites a chat whose first turn was a cancelled skill subagent.

title: terminal: avoid detached terminal listener leaks
body:
## Summary

- Prevents detached terminals from adding one theme listener and one configuration listener per instance.
- Eliminates listener leak warnings when agent and chat workflows create many detached terminals.
- Preserves live theme, configuration, and decoration updates through the existing centralized detached-terminal listeners.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Detached terminals skip `XtermTerminal` global service listeners because `TerminalService` forwards theme, configuration, and log-level changes to all detached instances. However, every detached terminal still creates a `DecorationAddon`, and that addon independently subscribed to the global theme and configuration services. Agent and chat workflows can keep enough detached terminal renderers alive to cross the listener leak threshold even though the main terminal listeners were already centralized.

### Implementation

`DecorationAddon` now accepts whether it should register global service listeners. Regular terminals retain the existing subscriptions. Detached terminals disable them, and the centralized `XtermTerminal.updateTheme()` and `updateConfig()` paths explicitly refresh decoration styles, layouts, capability listeners, and visibility.

A regression test constructs an addon with global listeners disabled and verifies that the theme service listener count does not increase.

### Behavior and constraints

- Regular terminal listener behavior remains unchanged.
- Detached terminals continue reacting to theme and relevant configuration changes through `TerminalService` existing centralized forwarding.
- Decoration refreshes remain owned by `DecorationAddon`; `XtermTerminal` only invokes the new public refresh entry points.
- Terminal disposal semantics and detached-terminal tracking are unchanged.

### Review context

The key review point is parity between the addon former direct subscriptions and the centralized detached-terminal refresh path. The centralized configuration handler already filters to terminal and decoration-related settings before calling `updateConfig()` or `updateTheme()`.

body: ## Summary Redesigns the Agent Customizations migration experience around a single **Migrations** entry and a unified migration homepage. - Groups pending migrations by **Your profile** and the active workspace. - Surfaces the existing supported migration flows for prompt files, VS Code user-data agents/instructions, and MCP servers. - Reuses the existing review pages, filtered to the profile or workspace selected from the homepage. - Supports skipping and re-including workspace migrations without changing files. - Provides scoped destination controls for file migrations. Workspace files recommend `.github` destinations, user files recommend `~/.copilot`, and MCP servers retain their fixed workspace-root `.mcp.json` destination. - Returns to the migration homepage after successful migrations and shows a success callout plus persistent, dismissible migration activity with source and destination paths. - Adds responsive dark, light, and high-contrast styling, keyboard/focus handling, Accessibility Help, and an Accessible View. ## UX details - The sidebar exposes one migration count rather than separate migration shortcuts. - Prompt-to-skill migrations are called out as higher risk because prompt-only metadata can be removed. - Completed profile/workspace groups receive a success treatment and no longer show destination controls. - Review-page lists remain virtualized but use simple, always-expanded sections. - Migration activity uses standard disclosure chevrons and remains scrollable within the modal. ## Out of scope This change intentionally does not add Chat Participants guidance, issue creation, agent-assisted verification, or optional multi-root workspace controls. ## Validation - Targeted migration dashboard, editor, configuration, and Agent Host discovery tests - Copilot customization-provider tests and built-in extension compilation - ESLint, CSS stylelint, and whitespace checks - Component fixtures covering overview, review pages, success/activity, skipped/completed states, narrow layouts, light/dark themes, and high contrast
